name: Medicine Checklist
description: A checklist for stocking and maintaining a well-organized home medicine cabinet with safe storage and current supplies.

items.text: General pain and fever relief suitable for your household
A reliable digital thermometer
Hot or cold packs for sprains and aches
Items for muscle aches or minor strains
Separate child-appropriate options if you have kids
items.note: Ask your pharmacist about suitable forms for children

items.text: Cold and cough comfort items for the season
Allergy relief for sneezing and itching
Antacids or stomach-settling items
Oral rehydration supplies for stomach upsets
Throat lozenges or soothing items
Assorted adhesive bandages and gauze
Antiseptic wipes or solution
Antibiotic or wound-care ointment
Medical tape and small scissors
Tweezers and disposable gloves
Check every item's expiry date
Discard anything expired or changed in look or smell
Make a list of items to replace
Restock anything running low
Set a calendar reminder to review again in six months
Keep medicines in a cool, dry place per the label
Store everything out of reach of children and pets
Use a locked cabinet or high shelf if children are around
Keep items in their original labeled packaging
Dispose of old medicine through a take-back program
This checklist is general information only and is not medical advice; ask your pharmacist or doctor about which items suit your household, correct use, and safe disposal, and follow their guidance
items.note: Keep prescription medicines tracked and stored according to your doctor's instructions

faq.q: What should a home medicine cabinet contain?
faq.a: Keep general basics such as pain and fever relief, cold and allergy items, antiseptics and bandages, a thermometer, and rehydration supplies. Tailor it to your household's needs and ask your pharmacist what to include.

faq.q: How often should I check medicine expiry dates?
faq.a: Review your cabinet at least twice a year. Remove anything expired or that has changed color, smell, or texture, and replace items so the cabinet stays ready when you need it.

faq.q: Where is the best place to store medicines?
faq.a: A cool, dry, locked cabinet away from heat and humidity is best. A steamy bathroom is often a poor choice. Keep everything out of reach of children and pets, and follow each label's storage instructions.

faq.q: How do I dispose of old medicine safely?
faq.a: Do not flush most medicines or toss them loose in the trash. Use a pharmacy take-back program or follow local disposal guidance, and ask your pharmacist if you are unsure how to dispose of a specific item.
